question: What will the first reported revenues after September 2026 be for the following companies? (Amazon)

calls.reasoning: Amazon guided Q3 2026 net sales of $197.0-202.0B (incl. ~80bp FX headwind); consensus ~$202.19B. Over the last 8 quarters actuals landed -0.7 to +3.7B vs the top of guidance (median ~+0.5B, mean ~+1.2B); the two most recent quarters beat the top by 3.0B and 1.6B as AWS accelerated to 37%. FX in Q3 was roughly neutral vs the July assumption (dollar weaker in Jul-Aug, stronger in Sep). Prime Day fell in Q2 2026, which depresses Q3's year-over-year growth and is already in the guidance. Median ~203.3B. No Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold market found. Exits below 198B or above 209B look very unlikely (~1% each), so no escape mass declared.

- Q3 2026 guidance (same 8-K): net sales $197.0-202.0B, +9-12% vs Q3 2025 ($180.169B); assumes ~80bp unfavorable FX; excluding Prime Day timing (Prime Day was in Q2 2026 vs Q3 2025), growth would be ~400bp higher. Op income guide $22.5-26.5B.
- Consensus revenue (MarketBeat, Oct 2026): ~$202.19B; EPS ~$1.96. Analysts expect AWS growth of 30-35% in Q3.
- Guidance history, top of range vs actual ($B): Q3'24 158.5 vs 158.9; Q4'24 188.5 vs 187.8; Q1'25 155.5 vs 155.7; Q2'25 164 vs 167.7; Q3'25 179.5 vs 180.2; Q4'25 213 vs 213.4; Q1'26 178.5 vs 181.5; Q2'26 199 vs 200.6. Actual minus top: -0.7 to +3.7; median ~+0.5, mean ~+1.2.
- FX (CNBC Sep 30 2026, StoneX): the dollar softened in Jul-Aug and rebounded in Sep (DXY ~98.6 -> ~101); EUR/USD ~1.14 at Sep 30. The Fed hiked on Sep 16.
- Capex raised to ~$220B for 2026; one Seeking Alpha piece cites a $496B backlog.
- Status quo: Amazon has not reported below the bottom of its guidance range in recent years.
- Resolves off the Q3 2026 earnings release (expected Oct 29 2026, after market close), total net sales as initially reported.
- Event window: quarter Jul 1 -> Sep 30 2026 (complete); report due Oct 29 2026; as of Oct 23 the quarter is 100% elapsed and the report has not been released.
- Searched for but did not find: Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold markets on Amazon revenue; segment-level consensus for NA/International.

calls.reconciliation: All three runs share the same evidence: the guidance, consensus and beat history. They differ only on small details: the guidance top for Q1'26 (it may not be exact, but it changes the beat distribution only slightly) and how much the September FX headwind matters (judgment; all three call it small/neutral). Medians already converge at 203.2-203.3B, and widths range 4-5B. I take a median of 203.2B with a 10-90 width of ~5.0B, consistent with the empirical beat range. No escape mass: falling below 198B would need a miss below the bottom of guidance, which has not happened recently; above 209B would need a ~7B beat, never seen.
